The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.
papers.tldr: PixelOneは、GUIグラウンディングのために、スクリーンショットからネイティブ解像度でクリックを直接予測するモデルで、教師からの空間知識を活用して精度を向上させ、83.8%の平均精度を達成しました。

papers.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a promising approach for scaling deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. However, existing MoE adaptations for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models suffer from significant computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of zero-shot capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose CLIP-FMoE, a novel approach that integrates MoE architecture into CLIP fine-tuning. Our method uses Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning, a pipeline that trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization. Additionally, we introduce a Fusion Gate mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves consistent improvements on downstream tasks while preserving zero-shot capabilities. Furthermore, our method demonstrates robust performance across varying context lengths, making it particularly suitable for diverse real-world applications.
papers.tldr: CLIP-FMoEは、Mixture-of-ExpertsアーキテクチャをCLIPモデルのファインチューニングに統合し、専門家の特化を加速するIsolated Constrained Contrastive Learningを用いることで、計算効率を維持しながら下流タスクの性能を向上させる新しい手法です。

papers.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents
papers.summary: Long-lived Web assistants require effective memory and retrieval mechanisms to access information from past user interactions. While these capabilities can be learned through specialized policies, it remains unclear whether specialists trained independently in different environments can be effectively composed without joint optimization. This paper investigates compositional transfer through policy distillation. Memory-writing and sequential retrieval policies are independently distilled from frontier-model action trajectories into 3B models and combined with a fixed answer generator without downstream training. On a LongMemEval-based benchmark, the distilled composition achieves 73.1% accuracy, compared with 36.2% for a composition of existing RL-trained specialists, and also outperforms the evaluated RL-trained compositions on PersonaMem-v2. Component ablations reveal that improvements in individual policies depend on their composition, highlighting the importance of cross-specialist compatibility. Further task-specific adaptation improves accuracy to 75.2% on LongMemEval through RL and 48.9% on PersonaMem-v2 through supervised distillation. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of independent specialist distillation for modular multi-agent systems. Source code and datasets of teacher-generated memory-editing and retrieval trajectories are released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
papers.tldr: 長期的なWebアシスタントにおいて、独立して訓練されたメモリとリトリーバルポリシーを組み合わせることで、効果的な情報アクセスが可能であることを示し、独立したポリシーの蒸留による構成が高い精度を達成することを明らかにした。

papers.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for spatial tasks such as navigation and manipulation, where they must infer geometry and object relationships from visual input in order to act correctly. Existing benchmarks usually test perception and reasoning in isolation, making it hard to tell whether failures come from visual understanding, downstream reasoning, or the bridge between them. We introduce VeriWorld, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification. For task families where all three channels are well-defined, we evaluate matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on the same instance, environment, and verifier; families without a clean visual/structured/combined split are reported separately. This design supports controlled comparisons of perception, reasoning, and their interaction. Using this setup, we uncover two diagnostic findings. First, models often perform much better when task-relevant information, such as object identity, current state, or target location, is given explicitly than when it must be read from the rendered scene, revealing a recurring visual-to-structure gap. Second, action-space and harness design can change outcomes even under the same task and information condition, showing that interaction protocol is itself a confounding variable. VeriWorld is open-sourced to support reproducible and fine-grained evaluation of spatial reasoning in VLMs.
papers.tldr: VeriWorldは、視覚言語モデル（VLM）のためのインタラクティブな3D環境における空間推論のベンチマークであり、視覚理解と推論の相互作用を明確に評価するための設計がなされています。このベンチマークを通じて、タスク関連情報の明示的提供がモデルの性能に与える影響や、アクションスペースの設計が結果に及ぼす影響が明らかになりました。

papers.title: EditGRN: Inversion-Free Image Editing by Source-Target Generative Synchronization
papers.summary: Text-guided image editing faces a persistent trade-off between preserving source content and realizing coherent target semantics. We explore this challenge through training- and inversion-free image editing based on discrete generative models. Existing inversion-free discrete editors primarily rely on post-hoc probability correction, creating a disconnect between local token-level adjustments and globally coherent semantic generation. To bridge this gap, we introduce EditGRN, a training- and inversion-free framework with trajectory-wide source-target generative synchronization in discrete space. EditGRN adopts a dual-branch design---the source branch constructs source references and the target branch generates the target image-enabling trajectory-wide synchronization between the two. Exploiting GRN's ability to recover clean tokens from arbitrary binary corruptions, the source branch directly constructs corrupted source states at each refinement step to extract useful editing features, without recovering a specific source-generation trajectory. The target branch synchronizes with the source branch through the same corruption schedule, fusing the corresponding source context with editable representations intra-model. By synchronizing source context with target generation along the entire trajectory, our approach faithfully preserves the background while producing high-quality edits that blend seamlessly with the surrounding scene through intra-model fusion. PIE-Bench show state-of-the-art performance on background preservation and text alignment across diverse editing tasks against continuous and discrete baselines.
papers.tldr: EditGRNは、トレーニングや逆変換なしで画像編集を行うフレームワークで、ソースとターゲットの生成同期を通じて、背景を保持しつつ高品質な編集を実現します。この手法は、従来の手法に比べて背景保持とテキスト整合性において最先端の性能を示しています。

papers.title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis
papers.summary: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. Methods that model scenes as sequences of object vectors learn spatial constraints implicitly, leaving collisions and boundary violations to losses or post-processing; semantic-map methods make occupancy explicit, but collapse instance and directional structure. We introduce RoomTokens, a sliced structured-token representation in which each token stores semantic class, instance-color identity, and facing field. This representation allows a scene to be generated as a discrete grid while preserving cues for instance grouping, orientation estimation, and 3D extent prediction. To learn the RoomToken distribution, we propose MDIRT (Masked Diffusion over RoomTokens), a masked discrete diffusion model that denoises semantic/instance-color/facing channels jointly with a shared cross-slice backbone. Architectural tokens are clamped as explicit floor- plan constraints, so the model samples furniture layouts that respect room geometry while retaining instance and object-attribute structure. Experiments on 3D-FRONT show that RoomTokens with MDIRT improve layout fidelity and physical consistency over sequence/vector- and map-based methods, suggesting structured spatial tokens as a practical choice for discrete 3D scene synthesis.
